section_summary.extract_value: The section reports inter-scale correlations for women in Zimbabwe and women in Britain, finding significant correlations between weight discrepancy and body appreciation in both groups and significant relationships of each with exposure to Western media. Fisher r-to-z tests indicated no significant between-group differences in these correlations, and in the Britain sample partial correlations controlling for length of residence showed exposure to Western media remained significantly correlated with weight discrepancy (r = .20, p = .018) and with body appreciation (r = -.22, p = .010).
section_summary.evidence_source: "As can be seen, among women in Zimbabwe, weight discrepancy and body appreciation were significantly correlated, and each of these variables was also significantly correlated with exposure to Western media. The same pattern of results was found for women in Britain... Using Fisher r-to-z transformations, we found no significant between-group differences on any of the correlation coefficients (all zs ≤ 0.26, all ps ≥ .794)... For women in Britain specifically... exposure to Western media remained significantly correlated with both weight discrepancy (r = .20, p = .018) and body appreciation (r = -.22, p = .010), once the duration of residency in Britain had been controlled for."
